name: Depot Dispatch
description: Assigns vehicles to routes and pulls them in for maintenance before they fail on the road. It owns the assignment table — which vehicle runs which route — and the maintenance bookkeeping: distance since service, scheduled downtime, and the utility.maintenanceDue warning that arrives early enough to route around. It does not drive anything: once assigned, movement.pathfinding_system and the vehicle's own movement components do the moving, and this component only hears about routes going away (world.routeAdded, world.routeBlocked) and service timers completing. A blocked route with vehicles on it triggers reassignment, not pathological waiting, because an idle fleet in a tycoon game is lost money the player should be told about. It does not own buying or selling vehicles — fleet growth is an economy decision — and it does not own what the vehicles carry; manifests and passengers board after assignment, not before.

inputs.name: serviceIntervalKm
inputs.description: Distance between required services. Short intervals make maintenance a real operating cost; long intervals make the depot a formality.

inputs.name: maintenanceDurationSeconds
inputs.description: How long a vehicle is out of service. Long enough that route coverage needs spare capacity — that is the tycoon puzzle this input creates.

inputs.name: allowAutoReassign
inputs.description: Whether idle vehicles may be auto-shifted to uncovered or blocked routes. Off for players who treat dispatch as the game itself.

outputs.name: uncoveredRouteIds
outputs.description: Routes with a schedule but no assigned vehicle — the list the expansion advisor and the efficiency score both consume.
